source: Youssef Rebhi, Map_layer/martian_map/layers/L5_poi/exports/poi_cards.json (NASA/JPL news and Curiosity blogs; positions = Curiosity waypoint on that sol). Nazca text checked by Malak's team on the NASA blog, 15 Nov 2026. Sources re-read on 15 Nov 2026 by Malak's team: contact text from Siebach et al. 2025 (GSA, doi 10.1130/abs/2025AM-10634); Altadena, Monte Grande and Nevado Sajama texts and open questions from the linked NASA pages. 'Take for the lab' lists are the team's suggestions.

sites.name: Sulfate unit to boxwork contact
sites.what: Curiosity crossed the contact from the Layered Sulfate unit into the boxwork-bearing rock on sol 4534 (7 May 2025), the start of the boxwork campaign. The boxwork rock is a friable, fine-grained mudstone with more Si and Al and less Mg and S than the sulfate unit.
open: Why are boxwork patterns found here and nowhere else on Mount Sharp?
Is the boxwork rock a separate unit bounded by this contact (an unconformity)?
How did the boxwork-bearing rock come to differ in chemistry from the sulfate unit below?
samples: Chip from each side of the contact (sulfate layer and boxwork bedrock)
Photo of the contact with a scale bar

sites.name: Altadena · first boxwork drill
sites.what: First drill sample of the boxwork campaign (8 June 2025). NASA found that the bedrock between the ridges has a different composition from other layers of Mount Sharp, and that white calcium sulfate veins came back here after mostly disappearing higher up.
open: Why were the ridges hardened into these patterns, and why only here?
Why did the calcium sulfate veins return in this layer?
Do the cemented ridges keep organic molecules or other signs of an ancient habitable environment?
samples: Chip of the bedrock, with a white calcium sulfate vein if you see one
Photo of the veins with a scale bar

sites.name: Monte Grande hollow · Valle de la Luna drill (44th hole)
sites.what: Boxwork hollow studied in Oct 2025. Curiosity drilled its 44th hole here, Valle de la Luna, to compare hollow and ridge.
open: Ridges and hollows differ only subtly in chemistry: what makes the ridges resist erosion?
How did such a wide network of ridges and hollows form?

sites.name: Nevado Sajama · ridge-top drill
sites.what: Ridge-top drill completed on sol 4718 (Nov 2025), drilled again as Nevado Sajama 2 (image sol 4803). Fine bright and gray veins here record fluids that went through the ridge, to compare with the Valle de la Luna hollow sample.
open: Did the fluids that left these veins make the ridges resist erosion?
How does the ridge rock compare with the hollow rock below (Valle de la Luna)?

sites.name: Nazca · 49th drill hole
sites.what: Block packed with disc- and needle-shaped forms the team reads as possible crystals; drilled on sol 5050 (Oct 2026). If they are crystals, they record the old environment.
open: Are the discs and needles really crystal forms?
Is today's mineral the original one, or did it change later?
samples: Block with many discs and needles, whole if small
Close-up photo of the discs with a scale bar
Chip of the plain rock around them, to compare
